title: Semantic versions and a lock for the standard

C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

items.title: A semantic version for the standard, beside the stamp it replaces
items.what: Today a project records `<commit-count>-<short-sha>` (e.g. 187-5a62e87) in .common-rules-version. It orders correctly and says nothing about what changed or whether catching up is safe. Add a VERSION file holding a semver, and define the bump rule: a mandatory Standard change is a MINOR bump, a change that breaks a project already following the rules is MAJOR, anything else -- a tool, a fix, wording -- is PATCH. Keep the commit-count stamp alongside it, because it is what orders two versions unambiguously.
items.done: VERSION holds a semver; the bump rule is written in CLAUDE-workflow.md; rulecheck reports both the semver and the count; a project's stamp records both.

items.title: The changelog is the source of the bump, and a test says so
items.what: The sponsor asked for the changelog to maintain the version going ahead. Derive the required bump from the CHANGELOG entries since the last release: any entry carrying `**Standard change (mandatory):**` forces at least a minor. A test fails when VERSION and the entries since the last release disagree, so the version cannot drift from what the changelog says happened.
items.done: A tool prints the bump the changelog requires and what VERSION says; the test fails on disagreement; both run in the merge gate beside bin/workflow-stamp --check.

items.title: A lock a project can trust: what it is aligned to, and what is pending
items.what: The sponsor asked for a lock. A project's .common-rules-version becomes a small lock file: the semver and count it is aligned to, the date, and the ids of the mandatory entries it has implemented. rulecheck then answers a sharper question than 'behind' -- which entries are pending, by id, and whether any of them is a MAJOR the project cannot adopt without work. Backwards compatible: a bare `<count>-<sha>` string keeps working and is read as a lock with no recorded entries.
items.done: A lock records the semver, the count and the implemented entry ids; an old plain stamp still validates; rulecheck names pending entries by id; tested on a fixture project with each shape.

items.title: Release 1.0.0 once nothing is pending
items.what: The sponsor: "release a baseline when the pending tasks are done". Cut 1.0.0 when every item in proposals 19-31 is done or on the back burner with its reason, the card reads ready, all twelve conformance checks hold, and the full suite is green on main. Tag it, write what a project adopting 1.0.0 gets, and say plainly what is NOT in it.
items.done: A git tag v1.0.0 on a green main; a release note naming what a project gets and what is deliberately excluded; the adoption handover updated to point at the tag rather than a moving main.

asks.quote: Can you version the common rule and release a baseline when the pending tasks are done. Use semantic version version and change Lock to maintain it going ahead
